issue.title: bind db engine and redis client to app for global usage

issue.body:
Hiya

I'm using the app lifecycle (on_startup) to dynamically modify a FastAPI app instance.  I notice that the scope['app'] is always being overridden. Which means that modifications in that happen in on_startup are lost by the time my endpoint handler is called.

starlette/applications.py is called multiple times during a request-response cycle.

```
    async def __call__(self, scope: Scope, receive: Receive, send: Send) -> None:
        scope["app"] = self
        await self.middleware_stack(scope, receive, send)

```

should this altered be to preserve an already set scope["app"] ?

i.e.
```
    async def __call__(self, scope: Scope, receive: Receive, send: Send) -> None:
        if "app" not in scope:
            scope["app"] = self
        await self.middleware_stack(scope, receive, send)

```

I notice that in starlette/routing.py scope["router"] is checked for existence before being set.
Is there a good reason for scope["app"] to be rewritten on each call?
